data.one_liner: Run on-device ML models and streaming LLMs using PyTorch ExecuTorch.
data.what_it_does: ExecuTorch Flutter provides a Dart API for loading and running ExecuTorch .pte models and streaming text generation models locally via dart:ffi. It handles native platform integration across Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and Web.
use_when: You need on-device machine learning inference using PyTorch models in Flutter.
You want to run streaming local LLMs like Gemma on mobile or desktop devices.
You require cross-platform support including web and desktop for AI workloads.
avoid_when: You only need basic cloud-based AI inference handled via hosted backend APIs.
Your model uses unsupported tokenizers like WordPiece or BERT-family tokenizers for text processing.
strengths: Supports all 13 ExecuTorch tensor data types.
Cross-platform support including Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and Web.
Includes experimental streaming LLM support with hardware acceleration backends like XNNPACK, CoreML, and MLX.
weaknesses: Requires managing large model and tokenizer files on the device.
Some backends like Vulkan and MLX are experimental or limited to specific platforms.
data.setup_notes: Configure native build options under hooks.user_defines.executorch_dart in pubspec.yaml and update minimum OS deployment targets for iOS and macOS if required.

alternatives.name: llamadart
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose llamadart if you specifically want to run Llama-based models using llama.cpp in Dart.

alternatives.name: tflite_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose tflite_flutter if your models are in TensorFlow Lite format instead of PyTorch ExecuTorch.
